supporting_observations.claim: The observed recurring HTTPS requests target updates.pixelforge-suite.com at 13:37:50, 13:42:31, 13:47:45, 13:53:13, 13:58:15, 14:02:29 and 14:07:46 UTC, consistent with an approximately five-minute interval.
Endpoint network records attribute each recurring connection to PID 5684, C:\Program Files\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe, connecting to the explicit proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080.
PID 5684 started at 13:37:43 UTC with the --background argument under NWD\leo.martins, with explorer.exe as its parent, and terminated at 14:08:08 UTC.

Six successful CONNECT tunnels each report 1,524 client-to-server bytes and 19,382 server-to-client bytes. The intervening 13:42:31 request received a 407 authentication-required response rather than a successful tunnel.

The correlated executable path, destination and cadence match the approved PixelForge updater behavior described in the supplied inventory. This supports closing the alerted periodic traffic as benign update checking rather than treating periodicity alone as malicious beaconing.

known_telemetry_limitations: Successful proxy records describe CONNECT tunnels, not decrypted application requests or response contents; they do not establish what was transferred inside HTTPS (T046-00101, T046-00157, T046-00177, T046-00182, T046-00192, T046-00219).
The supplied recurring PixelForge records span 13:37:50–14:07:46 UTC, not the entire approximate 13:30–14:10 alert interval (T046-00101, T046-00219).
Process creation and connection records establish the reported updater path and PID, but do not provide a binary hash or signature verification for pfupdater.exe (T046-00098, T046-00099, T046-00103).
claims_not_established: Malicious command-and-control or exfiltration is not established by the recurring tunnel metadata (T046-00101, T046-00157, T046-00177, T046-00182, T046-00192, T046-00219).
The updater binary's integrity and the exact HTTPS payload contents are not established by the process and tunnel records (T046-00098, T046-00101, T046-00103).
unrelated_findings: Separate account-use review: at 13:26:04 UTC, WS-SOKAFOR-01 recorded an NTLM network logon for administrator sam.okafor originating from WS-LMARTINS-01. Validate this use against the supplied administration restrictions; these records do not establish remote command execution or a connection to the periodic updater traffic (T046-00023, T046-00024).

Separate software-policy ticket: DropboxUpdate.exe /svc ran as SYSTEM on WS-LMARTINS-01, although Dropbox is outside the supplied approved cloud-storage inventory. Execution alone does not establish file synchronization or exfiltration (T046-00119, T046-00120, T046-00127).

Separate source-validation review: FILE-NWD-01 initiated a connection to WS-LMARTINS-01 TCP/135 at 13:31:24 UTC. Validate its purpose given the restriction on remote-administration sources; the connection records alone do not establish administrative execution (T046-00067, T046-00068, T046-00069).
